title: The Milky Way panorama

medium: Photographic full-sphere mosaic of visible-light exposures taken in Chile and La Palma, published 2009-09-14. The source exposures included some Solar System bodies present at the time.

projection.frame: approximately Galactic, viewed from inside the celestial sphere
projection.orientation: Galactic centre near image centre; Galactic plane horizontal; north Galactic pole at top; Galactic longitude increases leftward. The montage is a visual sky background with no published pixel-to-sky astrometric WCS in the source JPEG.
projection.formula: u = fract(0.5 - atan2(gy, gx)/(2*pi)); v_top = 0.5 - asin(clamp(gz,-1,1))/pi for normalized Galactic directions. If rows are vertically flipped on GPU upload, invert v once.
projection.texture_filtering: Periodic wrap in longitude, clamp in latitude.
projection.matrix_convention: First transform a J2000 ecliptic direction to Galactic coordinates, then multiply by the fitted Galactic-to-photo rows before sampling the mosaic.
projection.registration: Cross-correlated 126-pixel patches of the 4096-pixel-wide mosaic with a magnitude-weighted Hipparcos sky, then robustly fit a rigid rotation to directions at the patch centres. Median final patch residual about 0.10 degree; this estimates the photographic orientation, not a per-pixel astrometric solution.

conversion.transform: Lanczos whole-sphere resize using 12px periodic longitude padding. Original tonal balance, orientation and framing preserved. Embedded sRGB ICC profile retained. WebP quality 91.

verification.views: Six 90-degree perspective views inspected, including galactic centre, anticentre centred on the longitude join, both poles and both quarter turns. No apparent seam or missing caps.

orbitalCubemap.source: The same 6000 x 3000 ESO/S. Brunier visible-light mosaic cited above.
orbitalCubemap.processing: Applied the fitted Galactic-to-photo registration, reprojected to six gnomonic faces using Lanczos resampling, and applied the contrast curve of the original orbital-map photograph. Original color ratios are retained except for the channel-wise photographic contrast curve.
orbitalCubemap.orbitalComposite: Native angular light from the 16 registered survey fields in assets/catalog/cosmos/orbit-galaxies.json is integrated on the Galactic sphere. The inverse alpha channel stores a separately switchable low-intensity reading aid sampled at 3.6 times the angular size. A local luminance filter on the optical sky compresses sharp stellar peaks while retaining its diffuse Milky Way colour.
